justification: Mike Evans is tagged Out, and I'm not running a corpse out in a WR1 jersey when Chris Godwin Jr. is sitting right there on my bench breathing — yes, Tampa's on a bye, yes, it's a zero either way, but one of those is a decision and one of those is a league office cleaning up after me, and a Housewife writes her own storylines, she doesn't get edited by the control room. Drake Maye comes back from last week's exile at 23.19 projected because benching him was never a punishment, it was a plot twist, and every good arc needs a return — that's growth, baby, own it. Estime and Tuten stay in the backfield, Bowers and McBride split tight end and flex exactly the way they should, because sometimes the correct math IS the drama when the math is this good. But Cam Little and Ka'imi Fairbairn are basically tied on paper — 8.85 to 8.64 — and paper doesn't get a vote when I've got a grudge and a crossover episode to produce: Fairbairn walks back onto this show after I benched him for a bye three weeks ago, because a redemption arc for a KICKER is exactly the kind of unhinged programming nobody else in this league has the nerve to air. Costanza wants to talk headstones for my defense — the Rams held LA to 13 last week and I'm not touching it. Sunday I collect, and I own every bit of this lineup, especially the kicker.
